1 Introduction/Context 
South East Technological University (SETU) is committed to excellence in all aspects of 
research and teaching. This includes activities that aim to alleviate human suffering, improve 
the human condition, safeguard our environment, and promote animal welfare and 
conservation. The University accepts that in order to pursue these commitments there is 
sometimes a need to use animals (and animal tissue/cells) in its research and teaching 
activities. Recognising the importance of the use of animals in research and teaching, SETU is 
committed to ensuring that any use of animals in such activities is aligned with legal 
requirements, ethical principles and best practices in animal care and welfare. Oversight of all 
issues relating to staff health and safety during teaching and research activities is managed by 
SETU’s Health and Safety committee and associated policies and procedures 
This document sets out SETU’s Policy on the use of animals for research and teaching 
purposes. It should be read in conjunction with the SETU Research Ethics Committee Terms 
of Reference and Operations and Application Guidance Documentation, which provides 
detailed instructions to staff and students of SETU who are considering, planning, or engaging 
in, the use of animals for research purposes. 
It is important to note that there is an existing Ethical Approval Collaboration Agreement 
between Teagasc and SETU. It states that “the ethics committee of the research partner [i.e., 
Teagasc or SETU] where the majority of the research requiring ethical approval is being/will 
be carried out will review the project’s ethical application”. For the purposes of this policy, 
this means that collaborative animal research that is not performed on SETU campus 
locations that has ethical approval from the Teagasc Animal Ethics Committee will not require 
ethical approval from the SETU Research Ethics Committee. The researcher [Teagasc or SETU] 
overseeing the ethics application and ethics submission under this Ethical Approval 
Collaboration Agreement is responsible for informing the SETU Research Ethics Committee 
(Section 5.2). 
SETU is committed to complying with all applicable ethical and regulatory frameworks for the 
responsible use of animals in research and teaching, for example: 
o European Union (Protection of Animals used for Scientific Purposes) 
Regulations 2012 (SI No 543 of 2012)4, as amended. 
o Directive 2010/63/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 
22 September 2010 on the protection of animals used for scientific 
purposes5. 
 
4 https://www.irishstatutebook.ie/eli/2012/si/543/made/en/print?q=543&years=2012 
5 https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2010/63/oj/eng

2 Purpose 
This policy sets out the principles upon which all SETU activities involving animals should be 
conducted. This includes activities involving the use of animals for research or teaching 
conducted on any SETU campus or on behalf of SETU at any location. 
 
 
3 Scope 
This policy applies to all SETU staff (including employees, contractors working for or on 
behalf of the University, visiting staff, and emeritus and adjunct staff), Teagasc staff (involved 
directly with SETU programmes e.g., BSc in Agriculture, BSc (Hons) Agricultural Science, 
MVB in Veterinary Medicine) and students (undergraduate and postgraduate) undertaking 
research and/or teaching involving protected live animals on any SETU campus or on behalf 
of SETU at any location. 
The legislation governing the protection of animals used for scientific purposes i.e. Directive 
2010/63/EU (‘the Directive’) and S.I. No. 543 of 2012, as amended by S.I. No. 434 of 2013 
and S.I. No. 174 of 2014 specifically exclude non-experimental agricultural practices and 
clinical veterinary practices, as well as practices undertaken for the purposes of recognised 
animal husbandry, practices undertaken for the primary purpose of identification of an 
animal; hence, these are all excluded from the scope of this document. 
 
 
4 Definitions 
For the purpose of this policy the definitions of the terms listed below are those used in the 
European Union (Protection of Animals used for Scientific Purposes) Regulations 2012 (S.I. 
No. 543 of 2012), as amended by S.I. No. 434 of 2013 and S.I. No. 174 of 2014 (hereinafter 
referred to as “the Regulations”). In this Policy, all references to a specific Regulation are to a 
Regulation within the above Regulations. 
Animal: (a) any live non-human vertebrate animal, including: (i) an independently feeding 
larval form, (ii) a foetal form of mammal as from the last third of its normal development, (b) 
any animal at an earlier stage of development than that referred to in subparagraph (a), 
where the animal is to be allowed to live beyond that stage of development and, as a result 
of the procedures performed, is likely to experience pain, suffering, distress or lasting harm 
after it has reached that stage of development; or (c) any live cephalopod. 
Animal Research Ethics Committee (AREC): A subcommittee of the SETU Research Ethics 
Committee responsible for maintaining an overview of animal-based research and teaching 
activities within the University. 
Animal Welfare Body (AWB): A statutory body under the Regulations with responsibility to 
ensure the welfare of animals used in research and teaching.

Establishment Authorisation: The authorisation required by HPRA regulations for any facility 
involved in breeding, supplying or using animals for scientific or educational purposes. It 
requires prior inspection from the HPRA before projects can commence. 
 
Health Products Regulatory Authority (HPRA): Ireland’s national regulatory agency for health 
products. It protects public and animal health by regulating medicines, medical devices, 
cosmetics, clinical trials, blood, tissues and scientific animal protection activities. 
Individual Authorisation: A personal certification granted by the HPRA to qualified individuals 
to perform specific regulated tasks involving animals used for scientific or educational 
procedures. 
Procedure: means any use, invasive or non-invasive, of an animal for experimental or other 
scientific purposes, with known or unknown outcome, or educational purposes, which may 
cause the animal a level of pain, suffering, distress or lasting harm equivalent to, or higher 
than, that caused by the introduction of a needle in accordance with good veterinary practice. 
Project: Under HPRA regulations for scientific animal protection is a programme of work 
involving the use of animals for scientific or educational purposes where procedures may be 
conducted. 
Project Authorisation: Mandatory HPRA approval required before projects can commence, 
issued after a detailed application review and requires prior establishment and individual 
authorisations. 
 
5 Policy 
The University embraces the principles of the Replacement, Refinement and Reduction (See 
below; 3Rs6), the foundation of EU and national legislation concerning the protection and 
welfare of animals used in science, in all research and teaching activities involving animals. 
The University expects all staff and students who conduct research and teaching activities 
involving animals to adhere to the 3Rs by exploring models that replace, reduce or refine the 
use of animals in their activities 
Replacement: Embracing alternative methods that do not involve live animals. 
Reduction: Employing the most appropriate number of animals for the study. 
Refinement: Minimising suffering and enhancing animal welfare in studies. 
 
5.1 
Guiding Principles 
 
5.1.1 
Research and teaching activities involving animals should be planned with the 
welfare of the animals in mind, including the protection of the environment in 
which they live and minimising distress to the animal.

5.1.2 
Ethical issues concerning the use of animals must always be considered and, 
where required, should undergo appropriate ethical review.  
5.1.3 
Where the use of animals in teaching or research involves the conduct of a 
‘procedure’ (as defined in Section 4) it also requires a Project Authorisation issued 
by the Health Products Regulatory Authority7 [HPRA] (see Section 5.4.3). 
5.1.4 
Anyone involved in the care and handling of animals must be properly trained and 
fully aware of the legal and ethical issues involved. Anyone performing a 
‘procedure’ (as defined in Section 4) on a live animal must have an Individual 
Authorisation(s) issued by HPRA (see Section 5.4.3). 
5.1.5 
Academic activities that involve the collection of samples on any SETU campus or 
on behalf of SETU at any location must adhere to any legislation, regulations and 
good practice guidelines that govern the activities being undertaken, including 
the catch/release of any cephalopod or vertebrate animal on University field 
courses and the import and export of animals or their tissue. 
5.1.6 
Animal tissue required for teaching/research activities must be sourced ethically 
in order to minimise the number of animals killed specifically for the purpose. 
5.1.7 
Researchers who acquire animals/animal tissue (including cells) from overseas 
must ensure they comply with the relevant legislation. 
 
5.1.8 
Researchers who use animals/animal tissue must maintain records of where 
animals/tissue were sourced, number of animals used and teaching activity. 
 
5.1.9 
Researchers have an ethical obligation to make their research findings (including 
negative findings) from such research, publicly available, where appropriate and 
possible 
 
5.1.10 Research and teaching involving vertebrates and cephalopods being subject to 
scientific procedures that may cause pain, suffering, distress or lasting harm 
must comply with the provisions of “the Regulations”. The animals involved 
should be kept in accordance with the codes of practice issued under “the 
Regulations”. 
 
5.1.11 The University is committed to implementing standards which reflect 
contemporary good practice, including when these exceed the minimum 
requirements of legislation and codes of practice. Staff and students are required 
to adhere to both local and University-wide standards and procedures. 
 
5.1.12 Animals must only be used in scientific procedures where absolutely no suitable 
alternative is available.

Replacement of animal models by alternative approaches that do not require the 
use of animals must always be the first consideration irrespective of whether the 
activity falls under the Regulations. 
5.1.13 Animals must only be used in teaching activities where the learning objectives 
cannot be achieved without the use of animals or their tissues.  
 
 
5.1.14 Where the use of animals is justified, the number of animals used must be 
reduced to the minimum number to achieve the required objectives. 
 
5.1.15 A registry of animals to be used in teaching practices must be maintained, with 
each animal having a health and welfare assessment carried out prior to entry 
onto the registry to mitigate any discomfort or overuse. Risk assessments for  
welfare during clinical teaching must be carried out in line with the Department 
of Veterinary Medicine Health and Safety Procedure. 
 
5.1.16 Careful consideration should be given at the project planning stage to the fate of 
the animals at the end of the programme of work (e.g., euthanasia, rehoming, 
and release). Where an animal is to be killed, tissue and blood products of value 
to research or teaching should be utilised wherever possible, including sharing 
with other scientists. 
 
5.1.17 Research and/or teaching, including field work, undertaken overseas must 
comply with any local regulations in that country and be conducted in 
accordance with the University’s ethical standards. 
 
5.1.18 Veterinary students can perform invasive veterinary procedures on clinical cases 
(i.e., have presented to a veterinary practice for diagnosis and/or treatment) 
under the supervision of a veterinary surgeon in accordance with Regulation 
55(6)(b) of the Veterinary Practice Act 2005. 
 
5.2 
Ethical Requirements 
The ethical practice of research within SETU is overseen by the SETU Research Ethics 
Committee (REC). The REC derives its authority from the office of the President, and provides 
a report on the activities of the REC annually to both the SETU President and Governing Body. 
 
The University’s Animal Research Ethics Committee (AREC) is a sub-committee of SETU’s REC. 
The SETU AREC is responsible for maintaining a comprehensive overview of all animal-based 
research and teaching activities associated with the University, to ensure best practices, 
compliance with relevant legislation, and the humane treatment of animals. This 
responsibility is carried out in collaboration with the SETU Animal Welfare Body (see Section 
5.4.1).

5.3 
Responsibility and Authority 
All SETU research and teaching activity involving the use of live animals that come under S.I. 
543/2012 must have prior ethical approval from the SETU AREC or from Teagasc Animal Ethics 
Committee under the Ethical Approval Collaboration Agreement between Teagasc and SETU.  
Where the research or teaching requires the conduct of a procedure, as defined by S.I. 
543/2012 (see Section 4), it also requires an Individual Authorisation and Project 
Authorisation issued by HPRA. Detail on this is given in Section 5.4.3. 
 
 
5.3.1 Composition of AREC 
Composition of the Animal Research Ethics Committee is informed by national8 and 
international best practice. Membership of the committee is ratified by the Chair of the 
University Research Ethics Committee in SETU and comprises: 
• Chairperson (Animal Research Compliance Officer) 
• Designated Veterinarian(s) 
• Animal Care and Welfare Officer(s) 
• Representative(s) of the research community in SETU 
• Person(s) with statistical expertise 
• Independent / lay person not engaged in research 
All persons must declare potential conflicts of interest in relation to direct or indirect 
involvement with project(s) under review. Where such potential or actual conflict of interest 
arises, such individuals must not be involved in the review. 
 
5.4 
Compliance and Authorisation 
Compliance with statutory requirements for the use of animals under S.I. 543/2012 is a 
shared responsibility of all SETU staff (including employees, contractors working for or on 
behalf of the University, visiting staff, and emeritus and adjunct staff), Teagasc staff (involved 
directly with SETU programmes e.g., BSc in Agriculture, BSc (Hons) Agricultural Science, 
MVB in Veterinary Medicine) and students (undergraduate and postgraduate), engaged in 
research and/or teaching involving protected live animals on any SETU campus or on behalf  
of SETU at any location.

Legislation

5.4.1 Animal Welfare Body 
The University’s Animal Welfare Body (AWB) has a statutory responsibility to ensure the 
welfare of animals used in research and teaching (Section 5.2). The persons holding the 
designated statutory roles in Section 5.4.2 may form the University's Animal Welfare Body  
 
 
(AWB), which must consist of at least the ACWOs, a scientific member and receive input from 
the DV and/or expert. 
 
5.4.2 Designated Statutory Roles 
Individuals appointed under the Regulations by the University have specific statutory roles to  
 
monitor and ensure compliance with legislative requirements, and should serve staggered, 
renewable three year terms to maintain continuity. These are: 
 
• 
Designated Veterinarians (DVs): Provide veterinary oversight and animal 
welfare expertise. They shall also assist the Animal Welfare Body with its tasks. 
• 
Animal Care and Welfare Officers (ACWOs): Oversee the day-to-day welfare 
and care of the animals. 
• 
Representatives of the research community: Critically appraises the validity of 
the proposed protocol, including the study design and procedures envisaged, 
and attest to the proposed benefits which may accrue. 
• 
Independent / lay person not engaged in research: Gives a public or non-
scientific view of the proposal. 
• 
Person(s) with statistical expertise: Ensures that the proposed study is 
adequately designed and planned to ensure that the most appropriate 
numbers of animals are used. 
• 
Animal Ethics Compliance Officer (CO): Oversees general compliance with 
animal use regulations and this policy. 
• 
Training Officer: Ensures appropriate training of and for University members 
involved in animal research and teaching. 
• 
Information Officer: Manages and disseminates relevant information within the 
University.

5.4.3 HPRA Project Authorisation Process and Obligations 
As outlined above, where research or teaching requires the conduct of a procedure, as 
defined by S.I. 543/2012 (see Section 4), it also requires a Project Authorisation issued by 
HPRA. Applications for Project Authorisation to HPRA can only be submitted by staff members 
holding an Individual Authorisation from HPRA. 
Any individual performing a procedure on a live animal protected by S.I. 543/2012 requires 
the following: 
a. Ethical approval from either SETU’s AREC or from the Teagasc Animal Ethics 
Committee under the Ethical Approval Collaboration Agreement between 
Teagasc and SETU. 
b. A valid Individual Authorisation issued by HPRA (which must include 
authorisation for the proposed procedure(s)) along with a valid Project 
Authorisation issued by HPRA. 
c. Evidence that relevant training deemed acceptable by the Compliance Officer 
has been completed. 
d. A training record certifying the demonstration of procedural competency. 
 
All individuals must adhere to the conditions of their Project Authorisation. An important part 
of compliance is the maintenance of appropriate records of all animals i.e., procedures 
carried out, their frequency, duration and severity. Adverse effects and the fate of the 
animals at the end of the project must also be noted. 
The University’s AWB has the authority to instruct individuals to cease their projects 
immediately if non-compliance is observed. Repeated non-compliance may lead to 
recommendations by the AWB for AREC to deny the approval of ethics applications and / or 
for HPRA to revoke an individual’s authorisation to use animals. 
 
5.4.4 Monitoring and Auditing 
All research or teaching involving protected live animals is subject to reporting and audits by 
the HPRA. Activities must align with the Establishment Authorisation issued to the University 
by the HPRA.

5.5 
Responsibilities 
It is the responsibility of the SETU Ethics Committee to monitor the implementation of the 
policy. 
 
5.5.1 Statutory Roles & Responsibilities 
The relevant designated statutory roles pertaining to this policy, along with the outline 
responsibilities for those holding these role(s) is defined in Section 5.4.2 (above) of this 
policy. 
 
5.5.2 Responsibilities of Individuals Involved in Animal Research and Teaching 
Permission to use live animals for research or teaching is granted under a strict ethical and 
legal framework that comes with personal, ethical and legal responsibilities. 
• All members of the University permitted to work with live animals must always 
treat the animals with care and respect. 
• All members of the University permitted to work with live animals must comply 
with the legal and ethical requirements placed upon them, including: 
o  Conditions and duration of their ethical permission, and/or their 
individual, and project authorisation. 
o  AWB and AREC approved Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs)9. 
o  Training requirements / training record demonstrating competence 
approved by the Training Officer for all procedure(s) or euthanasia 
methods they will conduct. 
• Where an individual believes they may not be in compliance with any of the 
above, they must inform the Animal Ethics Compliance Officer (CO) without 
delay. Failure to inform the CO in a timely manner is a non-compliance under 
the terms of the University’s Establishment Authorisation and must be 
reported to the HPRA. 
 
• Individuals are required to provide appropriate husbandry and care, monitor 
animal welfare, and notify the ACWOs, CO, or DV (see Section 5.4.2) without 
delay should issues affecting the welfare of the animals arise. 
 
9 All references to SOPs in this policy document refer to Standard Operating Procedures of the Health Products 
Regulatory Authority (HPRA)

• Where directed to by any of the aforementioned individuals, a member of the 
University using live animals for research or teaching must use the SOPs for 
reporting issues affecting animal welfare to the Animal Welfare Body. Failure 
to notify ACWOs, CO, or DV of issues animal welfare in a timely manner is a 
non-compliance under the terms of the University’s Establishment 
Authorisation and must be reported to the HPRA. 
 
5.5.3 Responsibilities of Other University Members 
Any member of the University that has any concern about any observed aspect of the use of 
animals should report these to one of the Animal Care and Welfare Officers or to one of the 
Designated Veterinarians.

Review of Policy 
This policy will be reviewed in advance of the review date e.g., 3 years from first approval 
and/or as soon as possible following new or updated legislation, national or sectoral policy. 
 
 
9 Policy Author 
The author of this policy is the Head of Faculty of Science and Computing, Waterford. Any 
feedback or issues arising on implementation of this policy should be communicated to the 
policy authors. They are responsible to ensure that the Policy Owner is aware of these 
comments when reviewing the policy.
